signals.title_or_quote: [Feature]: Habit Tracker has no streak freeze / grace period — one missed day resets an entire streak with no recovery option
signals.why_relevant: User explicitly requests a grace period for missed days in habit tracking.
signals.drafted_reply: The distinction you're drawing between 'forgot to log' and 'actively missed' is exactly the right framing — the data model needs to treat those differently before any grace period UI makes sense. One practical approach is scoring against a weekly target rather than an unbroken daily chain, which sidesteps the binary reset problem entirely and maps better to how behavior-change research actually defines consistency. That also makes 'planned rest day' a non-issue since the week absorbs it naturally. I built an iOS app called Streakly that ships this as its core mechanic if you want to see one implementation: {APP_URL}.

rescore.why: The thread author is explicitly requesting a streak freeze/grace period feature for a habit tracker, which is the core mechanic Streakly is built around.
